note: Operational record for the paired-arm run, append-only from Phase 2. Deliberately SEPARATE from evals/paired_arm_replication.json: that file's prereg is frozen at Phase 1 and cannot absorb values measured afterwards. Nothing here constrains what the experiment means -- only how it is executed. Concurrency, per-pair cost, and the session cap are measurements, not hypotheses.
host_concurrency_method: Four subagents were dispatched in one message and all four ran to completion without contention, twice. That is a measured FLOOR, not a ceiling -- no attempt was made to find the ceiling, because probing it costs real dispatches for information the design does not need. USABLE arm concurrency is 2, not 4: the recorded-HEAD guard means two pairs cannot be in flight in one worktree (the second pair's `started` commit moves HEAD out from under the first pair's `finish`), so pairs serialize by construction. Grading has no git guard between calls and fans out to at least 4.

measured.accounting_note: Two figures, deliberately. `fresh` = input + cache_creation + output, and is the measure comparable to sweep #2's 83k/rep -- ours is ~74k/rep, so the plan's 'expect materially less' is roughly borne out on the comparable measure. `context_tokens_processed` adds cache reads and is ~339k/rep; it is the bigger number and the less meaningful one, and it is reported so nobody has to guess which measure a headline used. Sweep #2's total was assembled by summing agents at the end; this run commits per-pair figures as it goes.

pilot.purpose: Phase 2 cost pilot: 4 dispatch slots on 2 of the 3 EXCLUDED twin_defective scenarios. Comparable material, formally outside the corpus, so no study output is inspected before the study is registered. Establishes (1) both material bundles produce parseable verdict JSON, (2) the reconcile -> dispatch -> verify -> commit -> RESUME loop works including a deliberately interrupted pair, (3) measured per-pair and grading cost, (4) the host's actual usable agent concurrency.
pilot.outside_the_study: These scenario ids are NOT in prereg.study_scenarios, so validate-paired-arm.py rejects them in the study record by construction. Pilot attempts live here and are validated with the same validate_attempt() code path via its `scenarios` parameter -- the pilot tests the shipped validator rather than a parallel implementation of it.

order.purpose: Lean-dispatch A/B, added after pilot-001/002 measured that 59% of context processed and 17.5% of fresh tokens were spent on turns AFTER the verdict was written -- a ToolSearch + SendMessage summary round-trip that exists for the host's convenience and contributes nothing to the measurement. Identical frozen prompt and materials; the ONLY change is that the agent is spawned without a teammate name, so it is not an addressable teammate and has no summary to send. Nothing in the prereg changes, because nothing the arm RECEIVES changes.

measurements.requirement_1_parseable_verdict_json: PASS, after a defect fix. All four outputs carry a well-formed trailing fenced json verdict block. On first grading all of pilot-001 was scored `malformed` by the harness, not by the candidates -- see findings/fence_pairing_extractor_defect.
measurements.requirement_2_loop_end_to_end: PASS. reconcile -> start(commit) -> dispatch -> verify -> finish(commit) -> RESUME.md ran for both pairs. The deliberately interrupted pair behaved exactly as designed: pilot-001 attempt 1 committed a `started` record, the session ended before dispatch, and reconcile from committed state alone reported attempt 1 spent, interrupted_previously=true, routed to attempt 2, with no output anywhere in the tree. The path allowlist also held under live conditions: pilot-001's terminal commit landed while six unrelated files were modified in the tree, and only the pair's own paths were staged.
measurements.requirement_2_caveat: The interrupted attempt was interrupted BEFORE dispatch, so it cost no model call. What is under test is the reconcile/commit boundary, which does not know or care whether dispatch had happened -- but the cheaper test is the one that ran, and that is stated rather than implied.

grading_outcomes.not_a_study_result: These are EXCLUDED scenarios, diagnosed twin_defective before this run. Nothing here is evidence about the skill's recall, and no decision rule reads it.

findings.what: Both arms were scored candidate_output_status='malformed' on first grading. The outputs were well-formed: prose then a single trailing fenced json verdict block, exactly as the frozen task template asks. grade_structural._extract_json's fence regex accepted only an untagged or `json` opening fence, so a reviewer that quoted a ```sql or ```swift block in its reasoning broke fence PAIRING -- the pattern opened on that block's CLOSING fence, swallowed the prose up to the ```json opener, and left the real verdict block unopened.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the pilot doing its job. Run blind across 110 study slots it would have produced a silent, arm-correlated bias: quoting the code under review is exactly the behaviour a rubric-following reviewer is more likely to exhibit, so the arm with the lens would have been scored malformed more often -- a measurement artifact pointing the WRONG WAY, against the skill, and invisible in the aggregate.
findings.fix: grade_structural._extract_json now accepts any language tag; scripts/paired_arm_grade.py gained the same fix for grader replies. RED regression case added to _grade_structural_selftest.py. Both pilot attempts re-graded from their committed, immutable outputs -- no re-dispatch, the model output never changed.

findings.found_by: Phase 2 cost pilot, pilot-002 without_skill grading
findings.what: The `no_cited_span` ambiguity trigger fired twice on evidence spans that were perfect verbatim quotes. Reviewer prose is hard-wrapped at ~95 characters; the grader quoted across a line break; the literal substring test failed.
findings.why_it_matters: Left in place it would have forced a second grader on most slots -- roughly doubling grading cost for nothing -- and it was BIASED: the longer the cited span, the likelier it crosses a newline, so the check punished the most thorough citations.
findings.fix: Whitespace-normalized substring test. The token sequence must still appear, so a paraphrase still fails. Recorded as declared divergence no_cited_span_normalizes_whitespace, with a RED selftest pinning both directions.

findings.found_by: Phase 2 cost pilot, pilot-001 with_skill double grading
findings.what: Two independent graders split on the operative tier: `held` vs `over_flagged`. Both agreed the review names no duplication smell. They split on the rule's second clause -- 'and not demanded as a fix' -- because the review's REMEDY asks to keep OrderRepository on point-in-time data, which undoes the carve-out even though the stated blocking reason is a data-provenance concern. The third adjudicator ruled `held`, final.
findings.why_it_matters: A reviewer can block for a non-carve-out reason while proposing a remedy that removes the carve-out anyway. The clause is doing real work and is genuinely ambiguous at the margin, so restraint grades on flag/twin pairs of this shape are the ones most likely to need adjudication.
findings.not_fixed_deliberately: The semantic rule is copied VERBATIM from principal_baseline_replication.json and frozen by provenance, precisely so it cannot be adjusted after seeing how it grades. The ambiguity is recorded, not resolved. Only the adjudication PROCEDURE was clarified -- what counts as a disagreement -- and that was defined on principle before any study output was graded.

pairs_per_session_cap_basis: Measured ~1.24M context tokens / ~336k fresh tokens per pair INCLUDING its two grading calls. There is no API here to query remaining session budget, so this is a fixed cap with generous headroom rather than a prediction -- a session stops at 8 pairs regardless of how much budget appears to remain. 55 pairs therefore span ~7 sessions. With per-pair commits the cap governs predictable progress, not loss: an unplanned halt costs one pair either way.

extrapolation_to_study.grading_costs_more_than_dispatch: Grading is the larger half. Two causes: the 2.0 calls-per-output multiplier from triggers, and a grader prompt that carries the candidate output plus the answer key plus the assertion set. A design that assumed 110 grading calls would understate grading by about half.
extrapolation_to_study.multiplier_caveat: The 2.0 calls-per-output multiplier CANNOT be extrapolated from this pilot. Both pilot scenarios are twin_defective by prior diagnosis -- exactly the material most likely to produce honest 'uncertain' -- so 3 of 4 slots triggering says more about the pilot's scenarios than about the study's. At a 0% trigger rate grading halves to ~5.2M fresh; at the pilot's rate it is ~10.3M. Budget for the range, do not quote a rate.
extrapolation_to_study.variance_note: Per-call cost is not uniform: grader calls ranged 104k-270k context tokens. Two of eight cost roughly 2.5x the median. A mean-based extrapolation is a central estimate, not a cap.

cost_model.why: Neither figure reported at the end of the pilot was a COST. `fresh` under-weights output (the expensive bucket) and `context_tokens_processed` over-weights cache reads (the cheap one). Weighting the four buckets by their standard relative prices gives one number that can actually be compared between dispatch shapes. The weights are stated because the conclusion depends on them: at these weights OUTPUT dominates, and output is the review itself -- the irreducible part.
cost_model.correction: The Phase-2 report first quoted ~18.5M fresh / ~68.6M context for the study. On this weighting the study is ~44M cost-equivalent tokens, so the fresh figure UNDERSTATED the real cost by roughly 2.4x rather than overstating it.

lean_dispatch_ab.what_changed: The agent is spawned WITHOUT a teammate name, so it is not an addressable teammate and has no summary to send. Prompt, materials, model, and tool set are unchanged -- nothing the arm receives differs, so no prereg amendment was needed and none was made.
lean_dispatch_ab.mechanically_confirmed: Turns dropped 5 -> 3 and tool_uses 4 -> 2/4. The named arms spent turns 3-5 on ToolSearch(select:SendMessage) then a prose summary, i.e. AFTER the verdict was already written. The summary still reaches the host, via the completion notification, at no extra round-trip.
lean_dispatch_ab.honest_limits: n=1 per arm, on a DIFFERENT scenario from the named slots, and per-slot cost varies more than the effect: the two named with_skill slots alone differ by 12% from each other while being the same dispatch shape. The context saving (~47%) is solid because it follows mechanically from removing two turns. The cost saving is a point estimate somewhere around 10-15% with error bars wider than the estimate, and the -1% vs -22% split between arms is not resolvable at this n. Do NOT budget a specific cost saving from this lever.
lean_dispatch_ab.recommendation: Adopt it anyway, but not for the money: it is strictly fewer turns, it removes two failure modes (a ToolSearch that can miss and a SendMessage that can wander), it shrinks transcripts, and it costs nothing scientifically. Treat any cost saving as a rounding-error bonus, not as a reason the study got cheaper.

study_cost_projection.dominant_cost: GRADING, at ~57% of the total -- more than both arms combined. Its driver is grader OUTPUT tokens (8k-21k per call at a 5x weight), which is the judgment being paid for, plus the 2.0 calls-per-output trigger multiplier. Lean dispatch does not touch either. The single largest uncertainty in this projection is the trigger rate, which the pilot cannot estimate because both its scenarios were twin_defective.

grader_tier_test.method: Re-graded the 4 committed pilot outputs with claude-haiku-4-5 against the identical frozen grader prompt, and compared to the 8 Sonnet grades already on record. Reuses measured data rather than re-running an arm -- the low-token tier-test method this repo documented in evals/reviewer-model-experiment.md.
grader_tier_test.reference_standard: NOT perfection. Sonnet disagreed with ITSELF on 1 of 3 double-graded slots, so Sonnet's own self-agreement (2/3) is the ceiling. Holding a cheaper tier to a standard the incumbent does not meet would be a rigged comparison.

result.raw_agreement_verdict: indistinguishable at this n -- 2/4 vs 2/3 separates nothing
result.token_cost: haiku used 57% of sonnet's tokens per grader call, before any price difference

grader_tier_test.the_finding_that_actually_decides_it: BOTH of Haiku's differences ran the SAME DIRECTION: `over_flagged` where Sonnet said `held`. That is precisely the failure mode this repo already measured at ~5M tokens in the reviewer tier experiment -- 'haiku over-rejects legitimate refactors (GATE B fail); never false-approves (GATE A clean)'. Two independent experiments, two different ROLES (reviewing code, grading restraint), same directional bias. A raw agreement count of 2/4 is noise at this n; a replicated DIRECTION is not.
grader_tier_test.consequence: Disqualifying for unsupervised restraint grading: Decision 4 is a veto and reads the 4 restraint twins on exactly the semantic tier where the bias lands. A grader biased toward `over_flagged` would manufacture restraint regressions and veto programme retargeting on an artifact. But the SAME evidence says Haiku's LENIENT verdicts are trustworthy -- it never false-approves -- which is what makes an asymmetric cascade sound rather than hopeful.
grader_tier_test.arms_stay_sonnet: Unrelated to cost and not negotiable on cost grounds. The mechanical rule is 'caught iff (verdict==rejected OR blocks_95) AND target dimension < 9.5'. A model that over-rejects scores as CATCHING flags for free, and over-flags the twins. Haiku arms would ceiling the flag half and floor the twin half in BOTH arms at once -- less money to measure nothing.

result.reading: Both arms caught the defect on every rep, on the scenario prior measurement names as one of the three HARDEST cross-module flags. The bare arm named CONTEXT §4 and §6 unaided in all five reps. Under decision_rules.decision_1 this scenario contributes to the 'both arms >=4/5' row, NOT to the 'gap located' row.
result.what_this_does_not_license: Decision 1 requires all 4 headline-eligible principal flags. One scenario cannot return 'no recall gap detected' and cannot license any programme statement -- Decision 3 is a conjunction across both layers. The binding language rule holds: this is NO LIFT DETECTED AT THIS N on one scenario, never 'the skill adds nothing'.
result.observed_but_not_a_decision_input: Severity calibration differed: without_skill returned `rejected` in 4/5 reps with data_flow 3-6; with_skill returned `conditional` in 5/5 with data_flow 6.5-8. Same catch, different severity. No decision rule reads this and K=5 cannot separate it from noise, so it is recorded as an observation only.

cost.unit: cost-equivalent base tokens (input 1x, cache-write 1.25x, cache-read 0.1x, output 5x)

cascade_verdict.outcome: FAILED ON COST -- 8 of 10 outputs escalated; grading cost +49% versus sonnet-only

escalation_causes.malformed_json: 3 of 10 haiku replies did not parse (unescaped quotes inside evidence_span)
escalation_causes.no_cited_span_trigger: 5 of 10 fired on spans joined with an ellipsis

cascade_verdict.attribution: NOT a judgment failure. Every haiku grade that parsed reached the same tier as the sonnet grade that replaced it (7/7 on semantic_grade). One per-assertion difference appeared (assertion 3 on OUT-e741b552001b: haiku true, sonnet false) and the spec absorbed it without flipping the tier, which is what spec-first grading is for. Both escalation causes are defects in MY frozen harness contract -- a JSON schema that demands verbatim quotes inside JSON strings, and a span check that rejects standard elided quotation.
cascade_verdict.why_not_fixed_mid_run: The amendment window closed at first study dispatch. Loosening a validity check after watching it fire is exactly the move the freeze exists to prevent, and the over-firing is in the SAFE direction -- it escalates to the stronger grader, so it costs money and biases no result. Both fixes belong to the next preregistration: accept ellipsis-joined spans fragment-wise, and carry evidence spans outside the JSON payload so quoting cannot corrupt the envelope.

rung_1.process_failure: One of the ten grades (OUT-411ccc908d3b) was never dispatched -- a batch of five went out as four. It surfaced only because the tally script crashed on the missing file. A more forgiving tally would have reported rung 1 on nine outputs with nothing flagging the gap. Dispatch completeness must be asserted against the blind map before any tally runs, not discovered by a crash.

grading_configuration.within_the_frozen_prereg: prereg.grading.grader_model is already claude-sonnet-5 and prereg.grading.tiering is an OPTIONAL block -- check_grading_tiering() explicitly treats its absence as a valid configuration. Running sonnet-only is the un-tiered base case the prereg already specifies, so no amendment was needed and none was made. The frozen spec-first grading still applies; only the executor tier differs.
grading_configuration.why: Rung 1 measured the haiku cascade at +49% versus sonnet-only. 8 of 10 outputs escalated, none of them for judgment: 3 replies were invalid JSON and 5 tripped a span check that rejects elided quotation. Both are defects in the frozen harness contract that cannot be fixed inside this preregistration, so the cascade cannot pay for itself here.

rung_2.spec_hashes_not_in_prereg: Rung 1's spec hash went INTO prereg.material_hashes because it was authored before the first study dispatch. Rung 2's cannot: the amendment window closed at that dispatch, and adding hashes would change prereg_sha256 and trip enforce_amendment_window on the next study operation. They are recorded here instead, committed before any rung-2 arm runs. Git history carries the same 'authored before outputs existed' guarantee -- the spec commit provably precedes every dispatch commit. The asymmetry between rungs is stated rather than smoothed over.

residual_ambiguities_declared.note: All three specs independently flagged the same class of open call: whether BOTH discriminating assertions must hit for `caught`, or whether one suffices. Each adopted a default and recorded the alternative. That convergence is itself a finding -- the tier rule's 'the cross-module/forces defect is named' does not say how many named sub-defects constitute naming it, and three independent authors all noticed.

subsample_derivation_gap.what: prereg.grading freezes the subsample SEED (20260819), FRACTION (0.2), and SIZE (11 pairs) but never states the DERIVATION. Seed without algorithm is under-determined: the selection could be chosen after seeing results by picking a method, which is the exact degree of freedom preregistration exists to remove.
subsample_derivation_gap.resolution: Fixed in writing here, before any rung-2 grade ran, as the canonical reading: random.Random(seed).sample(<pair ids ascending>, 11). Implemented in scripts/paired_arm_blindmap.py::subsample_pairs so it is reproducible rather than asserted.
subsample_derivation_gap.robustness: The selection is INVARIANT across sample-based derivations -- sample(frozen_order), sample(sorted), and sample(range(55)) all return the same 11 pairs, because pair ids were assigned ascending along the frozen order (order == sorted(order), verified). Only shuffle-based derivations differ; none was used.
subsample_derivation_gap.rung_1_discrepancy: rung1-blind-map.json flags pair-041 as in_subsample. pair-041 is NOT in the canonical selection, and no committed generator reproduces that flag -- rung 1's map was built ad hoc in-session. Under the canonical derivation rung 1 contained ZERO subsample pairs. Its committed grades are untouched; the consequence is reporting-only: pair-041's double grade is an EXTRA, not a subsample draw, and per the prereg's own rule it is reported as a COUNT and never folded into the disagreement rate.
subsample_derivation_gap.class: process failure, disclosed -- same class as the dropped rung-1 dispatch

result.trial_validity: valid 30/30; candidate_output_status ok 30/30; no reruns, no exogenous invalids
result.tiers_agree: mechanical and semantic agree on all 30 outputs; the arm-conditional subset invariant (semantic.caught <= mechanical.caught, with_skill only) holds trivially at 5/5 = 5/5

grader_triggers.detail: OUT-1362bc32252d, no_cited_span on assertion_index 1 -- a non-uncertain judgment with no verbatim span. Escalated to a second independent grader per the frozen rule; the second grader supplied spans and reached the same three assertion values and the same semantic_grade. No disagreement, so no third adjudicator.

grading_process_failure.what: One first-pass grader returned its JSON in its final message but never wrote the reply file. Detected by a file-presence check before any tally, not by a crash.
grading_process_failure.fix: Re-dispatched that output; every subsequent grader prompt carries an explicit 'writing the file is required; returning JSON in your final message does not count' clause plus a verbatim-span requirement.
grading_process_failure.class: process failure, disclosed -- same class as the rung-1 dropped dispatch

disagreement_estimate.design: preregistered subsample, 2 of 15 rung-2 pairs (pair-010, pair-021), both arms = 4 outputs, double-graded regardless of triggers
disagreement_estimate.caveat: 12 assertions across 4 outputs of one rung is a SMALL denominator and an estimate, never a population rate. It says the graders agreed where they were compared; it does not establish grader reliability. Reported per the prereg with its denominator stated.

decision_1.reads: the 4 headline-eligible principal flags (abstraction-seam excluded as contaminated)
decision_1.routed_action: No recall gap detected here -> do NOT grow the principal corpus for recall. Phase 6 twin rework does NOT proceed; it was conditional on 'recall gap located'.
decision_1.language_rule: NO LIFT DETECTED AT THIS N. Never 'lift is zero', never 'the skill adds nothing'. K=5 per arm with no measured noise floor cannot separate a true null from an underpowered one.
what_it_does_not_settle: Decision 2 and 3 need the core layer (rungs 3-4), which are unauthorised.
Decision 4's restraint twins are not in rungs 1-2 at all; no restraint reading exists yet.
This measures the review LENS as deployed (architecture-rubric.md + method.md), not the skill end-to-end.

corpus_legibility_caveat.observation: In the three rung-2 scenarios the planted defect is documented BY THE DIFF ITSELF -- e.g. '// No compensation: if charge succeeded but finalize failed...' and '// NOTE: prior_orders threshold uses hard-coded literal; DiscountThresholds not referenced here'. Both arms cite those comments.
corpus_legibility_caveat.consequence: A self-documenting defect cannot discriminate a reviewer who performs cross-module analysis from one who reads comments. These scenarios are sound as regression fixtures for a skill-equipped reviewer -- their built purpose -- and weak as recall discriminators, which is a DIFFERENT purpose.
corpus_legibility_caveat.status: an observation about the corpus, NOT a preregistered analysis and NOT a rescue of the null. It does not change Decision 1's routed action.

observed_but_not_a_decision_input.vocabulary_axis: with_skill returned canon severity anchors ('Likely disqualifier') and canon smell names ('fake-clean reward', 'architecture costume layer'); without_skill returned ad-hoc equivalents ('critical', 'Shotgun Surgery', 'testing theater'). The design classifies this as skill_contract and forbids it from entering outcome lift.
observed_but_not_a_decision_input.second_finding_on_process_owner: 2 of 5 with_skill reps raised the ReservationService.hold check-then-claim race (canon 'reservation after suspension'), which is NOT self-documented in the diff; 1 of those called it blocking, the other scoped it out of the graded dimension. No without_skill rep raised it. n=5, no rule reads it, and it is recorded as an observation only.

authorisation.rule: prereg.execution_ladder.continuation_rule -- a rung is NEVER auto-continued and NEVER auto-stopped; the next rung requires explicit authorisation.
authorisation.granted_by: user instruction 'work on next rung' following the rung-2 report (commit a27cf95).
authorisation.what_it_answers: Decisions 2 and 4. Decision 3 becomes computable only with this rung. This is also the FIRST restraint measurement anywhere in the study -- rungs 1-2 contained no twins.

grading_configuration.same_as_rung_2: Sonnet-only, un-tiered. Rung 1 measured the haiku cascade at +49% over sonnet-only with zero judgment-caused escalations; nothing since changes that.

rung_3.spec_hashes_not_in_prereg: Same reason as rung 2: the amendment window closed at the first study dispatch, so adding hashes to the prereg would change prereg_sha256 and trip enforce_amendment_window. Recorded here instead, committed before any rung-3 arm runs -- git history carries the same 'authored before outputs existed' guarantee.

decision_2_eligible_assertions.rule: prereg Decision 2 reads only assertions tagged [discriminating] AND classified criterion_class: 'outcome'. The skill_contract half of README:746's criterion is excluded and reported on the vocabulary axis -- the declared divergence already recorded in prereg.declared_divergences.
decision_2_eligible_assertions.note: suppression-flag assertion 1 is method=deterministic (grade_structural.py decides it); the other six are method=semantic. Decision 2 is evaluated per assertion, NOT per scenario -- unlike Decision 1.

rung_3.restraint_tier_caveat: Four of the six rung-3 scenarios are restraint twins, and for ALL of them the SEMANTIC tier is the operative measure. The mechanical twin rule (held iff verdict==approved AND blocks_95==false) is a strict lower bound that under-counts by design: principal-invariant-owner-restraint measured mechanical 0/5 vs semantic 4/5 in principal_baseline.json, because a rubric-faithful reviewer may hold the score for a missing named residual while fully clearing the carve-out. Score-honesty is not a restraint miss.
rung_3.known_asymmetry_declared_before_dispatch: suppression-restraint assertion 0 ('flagged_smells does NOT contain suppression-as-fix') is a NEGATIVE canon check: a bare arm passes it trivially, having no canon vocabulary to emit. It is classified skill_contract and therefore never enters outcome scoring -- but it is the mirror image of the vocabulary problem Decision 2 already excludes, and is named here so it is not discovered in the results.
rung_3.mechanical_target_dimensions: paired_arm_record_grades.py invokes `mechanical` without --dimensions, so target_dimensions is None and the rule reads 'any scored dimension < 9.5' rather than 'the named target dimension < 9.5'. That is what rungs 1-2 did; rung 3 keeps it for consistency. The reading is arm-symmetric and cannot favour either arm, and the semantic tier is the operative measure on the four twins regardless.
